There is gradient normalization with elementwise sign for l_infinity.
There is a momentum factor of 0.9.
There is an initialization with uniform random perturbation.
An l_{infinity} ball is computed around non-normalized inputs.
Given an input x and text prompts t_1, ..., t_k, the ith logit of the classifieris computed as the cosine similarity of output of the image encoder on x and the output of the text encoder on t_i.
Given a label y, the loss is correctly computed as the cross-entropy loss as in equation 1 of section 3.2.

For each training sample x_i, the worst-case perturbed sample z_i is found using PGD by maximizing the cross-entropy loss against label y_i within an l_{infinity} ball of radius epsilon around x_i, where x_i is the non-normalized input.
The cross-entropy loss is computed for each z_i against its corresponding label y_i.
For each batch, the loss is computed by summing these individual losses over all samples in a batch from the training set and taking their mean.
The model parameters are updated using gradient descent on this loss.

Given an image encoder phi, image x and constant epsilon, the loss is the max of ||phi(z) - phi_{Org}(x)||_2^2 over perturbations z of image x satisfying ||z - x||_{\infty} \leq epsilon, where phi(z) and phi_{Org}(x) are the (non-normalized) feature embeddings produced by the fine-tuned and original CLIP vision encoders respectively, as in equation 3. Here, phi_{Org}(x) is frozen.
The loss is summed over the samples in a batch, and their mean is taken.
